To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Toxoplasmosis, an important disease of immunocompromised patients, can cause a relapse in immunocompetents.
Toxoplasmosis in immunocompetents can be diagnosed by measuring IgG and IgG antibody titers, but not by measuring IgM antibody titer.
Toxoplasmosis is an infection that can cause serious problems in people with weak immune systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of antibody in the immune response to Toxoplasmosis.
the development of a novel method for detecting the presence of Toxoplasmosis in immunocompromised individuals.
the development of a novel diagnostic method for cerebral tachyzotite growth in immunosuppressive patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
IgG and IgM antibody titres increase following challenge infection in chronologically infected mice.
Toxoplasmosis is not a benign condition.
the increased antibody titers in immunocompeten individuals chronically infected may be a good indicator suggesting cerebral growth of tachyozites.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IgG and IgM antibody titres are not useful for the detection of cerebral tachyozyte growth, but IgA antibody titres are useful for this purpose.
the antibody titer of IgG and IgM in the sera of immunocompromised patients with cerebral proliferation of Toxoplasmosis gondii is significantly higher than that of immunocompetant patients.
the IgG antibody titer in sera of immunosuppressed individuals with cerebral tachytozoite proliferation during the chronic stage is significantly higher than that of immunocompetents.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of IgG and IgM antibodies in serum is a useful indicator of a current infection with T. gondii, and that IgM is a better indicator than IgG.
the IgA and IgG antibody responses are associated with parasite burden in the brain, and that the IgM response is not.
IgG and IgM antibody titres do increase in immunocompetents during chronic stage of toxoplasmosis, but IgA antibody titres remain stable.
